newsitem.title: DUBAI: HORSE RACING-COUNTDOWN TO DUBAI WORLD CUP BEGINS.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-COUNTDOWN TO DUBAI WORLD CUP BEGINS.

text.p: The countdown to the Dubai World Cup has begun with organisers of the world's richest horse race announcing on Wednesday they had shortlisted 31 nominations.
Those invited to compete in the second edition of the $4 million race to be held on March 29 include what are being billed as the best horses from all corners of the globe.
With Cigar, the winner of the inaugural race last year, retired, the main attraction will be centred around Helissio, Key of Luck, Gentlemen and Singspiel.
"We have sent invitations to the best of the horses and once we receive the confirmation we will select 14," said Michael Osborne, chairman of the organising committee.
"We has received 115 nominations for the race and of that we are inviting the best 31," he said.
Among those invited are France's Helissio, rated as the best three-year-old in the world with an international classification rating 134 last year.
Winner of the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe in 1996, Helissio is already in Dubai, fine-tuning for the race which has $2.4 million at stake for the winner.
Key of Luck, owned by Sheikh Saeed bin Maktoum, improved dramatically last year. He won a support race in the Dubai World Cup with a time that beat Cigar's.

Gentlemen, the Argentine horse hailed as a new Cigar in the making, was sent to California for the 1996 season and performed extremely well, winning the Bay Meadows Handicap, the Citation Handicap and the Native Diver Handicap.

Singspiel, owned by the UAE's Sheikh Mohammed, is also being tipped as one of the favourites. Winner of the Japan Cup, where he beat top class horses such as Fabulous La Fouine, Helissio and Pentire, Singspiel has won his Eclipse award as older turf champion in North America.
The invited horses, with country of breeding in brackets are:

Annus Mirabilis (France), Bijou d'Inde (Britain), Carling (France), Donna Viola (United States), Doriemus (New Zealand), Editor's Note (United States), Even Top (Ireland), Flemensfirth (United States), Formal Gold (United States), Gentlemen (Argentina), Gothenberg (Ireland), Helissio (France), Hokuto Vega (Japan), Instingood (United States), Juggler (Australia), Key of Luck (United States), Luso (Britain), Marlin (United States), Mecke (United States), Montjoy (United States), Mt. Sassafras (United States), Needle Gun (Ireland), Sandpit (Brazil), Savinio (United States), Singspiel (Ireland), Siphon (Brazil), Sorbie Tower (Ireland), Talloires (United States), Tamayaz (Canada), Tamhid (United States) and Victory Speech (United States).
